title: AutoSim: A Self-Improving User Simulator for Conversational Search Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.28054v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: User simulators promise to evaluate conversational search systems at a scale human studies cannot reach, but only if their behavior is realistic enough to trust. We study AutoSim, a conversational-search user simulator whose relevance judgments rank a controlled pool of retrieval systems in agreement with NIST across three TREC iKAT years (Kendall's $\tau$ of $0.66$, $0.91$, and $0.91$; all $p{\le}0.002$), an agreement that survives removing its persona. AutoSim self-improves against a held-out signal from real users, and we find that fine-tuning its weights makes it behave like real users, which in turn gives a more accurate estimate of how well a system serves them. translated_title: AutoSim：一个用于会话式搜索评估的自我改进用户模拟器
translated_abstract: 用户模拟器有望以人类研究无法企及的规模来评估会话式搜索系统，但其前提是模拟行为必须足够真实可信。我们研究了 AutoSim——一个会话式搜索用户模拟器，其相关性判断在三个 TREC iKAT 年份中对一组受控检索系统的排序与 NIST 保持一致（Kendall's τ 分别为 0.66、0.91 和 0.91；所有 p ≤ 0.002），且这种一致性在移除其人格设定后依然保持。AutoSim 利用来自真实用户的保留信号进行自我改进，我们发现对其权重进行微调能使其表现得像真实用户，从而更准确地估计系统对真实用户的服务效果。要达到这种效果，仅靠提示工程是不够的：在区分真实与模拟用户会话时，我们尝试的所有提示方法都无法使保留集上的真实-模拟分类器的 AUC 降至 0.85 以下，而微调权重则将其降至 0.45，此时无论是……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: AutoSim 是一个会话式搜索用户模拟器，它通过真实用户信号微调权重实现自我改进，模拟行为逼真到难以与真实用户区分，且其相关性判断与 NIST 高度一致，从而能够可靠地大规模评估会话式搜索系统。
en_tdlr: AutoSim is a self-improving user simulator for conversational search that, through weight fine-tuning on real-user signals rather than prompting, behaves indistinguishably from real users and produces NIST-consistent relevance judgments, enabling reliable large-scale evaluation of conversational search systems.
